name: StreamingChurch.tv
shortDescription: A US church livestreaming platform with website and social streaming, video hosting and published plans for different broadcast needs.
suitableContexts: Teams wanting a trial before selecting a livestream provider

pricing.summary: StreamingChurch.tv publishes US-dollar Social Embed, Basic, Premium and Platinum plans, from US$19 to US$179 per month. Its plans describe unlimited audience and bandwidth; ask whether these plans and terms are available to a UK church.
pricing.trialDetails: The supplier advertises 30 days free with no card or activation charge.

support: Phone, chat and email support seven days a week stated by supplier

editorial.assessment: StreamingChurch.tv has a clear published trial and entry price, making it a viable product to put through a real service test. It is US-focused, so do not assume its published dollars, support arrangement or payment terms translate directly to a UK church.
bestFor: Churches that want to test a dedicated church streaming service
Teams comparing a modest entry tier with more advanced hosting needs
strengths: Published plan ladder and stated seven-day support
limitations: Ask the supplier about UK data, payment and contracting details

procurementVerdict.problem: Churches that want to test a dedicated church streaming service

longForm.verdict: StreamingChurch.tv is a practical candidate for a time-bounded comparison because it states a 30-day free period and a simple four-plan ladder. Use that period to test the complete viewer journey on the church website, not only whether a signal reaches Facebook or YouTube.

decisionLens.heading: A livestream is part of the congregation’s welcome.
decisionLens.text: The landing page, sound, captions or chat approach, archive and volunteer response all shape an online visitor’s experience. Choose the system that the team can operate calmly during a normal service, not the one with the longest feature list.

sections.heading: A trial that tests the ministry workflow
sections.question: What should be tested in thirty days?
paragraphs: Test a normal service and a realistic failure scenario: late volunteers, a changed service time and a poor connection. Review the viewer page on phone and desktop, then make sure recordings are placed where regular viewers expect them.

The supplier describes plan differences and unlimited audience and bandwidth. Confirm the exact archive, destination and support allowances that apply to the chosen plan rather than relying on a headline claim.

userFeedback.summary: This profile does not use an independent review score. It is based on StreamingChurch.tv’s public product and plan information.
themes: A no-card trial makes operational testing possible.
The decision should include website and volunteer workflow, not just broadcast delivery.
userFeedback.caveat: Supplier statements describe its own offer and do not establish UK availability, local support cover or local data arrangements.

faq.question: Does StreamingChurch.tv have a free trial?
faq.answer: The supplier advertises 30 days free with no card or activation charge. Check current plan eligibility before registering.

faq.question: How much is StreamingChurch.tv?
faq.answer: The supplier lists plans from US$19 to US$179 per month. Confirm which features and terms apply to the tier you need.

faq.question: Is StreamingChurch.tv UK-focused?
faq.answer: The reviewed supplier material does not describe a UK-specific offer. Ask about contracting, support timing and data arrangements directly.
